hypothesis: Per the plateau diagnosis (probe on node 10) and the ensembling guidance to pick structurally different mechanisms, combine the current-best plain bilinear BPR-FM (negative_sampling lever, 0.6041) with a BPR-trained DeepFM (adds an MLP over the same field embeddings — model_architecture lever, scored 0.6037 standalone in iter 7) in one run_model() call: train both on the same BPR pairwise objective, z-score-standardize each model's valid-split scores, and average. Since the two score functions differ in mechanism (pure bilinear interactions vs. bilinear+non-linear-MLP), their errors should be less correlated than the same-architecture ensembles already tried (e.g. iter 17's near-identical-FM ensemble), so averaging should reduce variance across the small informative-user pool enough to edge past the ceiling both hit individually.
reflection: The probe confirms the primary metric is genuinely bottlenecked by a small pool of "informative" users (only ~58-64% of valid/test users are label-mixed, median 4-5 rows/user), which explains why six structurally different mechanisms landed within 0.002-0.007 of each other — there's a hard ceiling on how much any single model can move the metric given how little rankable signal most users provide. That's a fundamental noise-floor issue, not something a 7th single-mechanism tweak will fix; the highest-leverage remaining move is variance reduction via ensembling two genuinely different mechanisms already validated separately.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since GAUC aggregates over many more mixed-label users/pairs (variance reduction from averaging two structurally different scorers helps a broad, noisy ranking signal) while nDCG@5 is already near-saturated for the majority of users with <5 valid rows and can't move much regardless.
